sections.normalized_html: Given that [MATH: x=-2] is a solution to the equation [MATH: x^3+8 = 0,] find the remaining solutions.
sections.readable_text: Given that [MATH: x=-2] is a solution to the equation [MATH: x^3+8 = 0,] find the remaining solutions.

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: f(x) = x^3+8.] Since [MATH: x=-2] is a root of [MATH: f(x),] then according to the factor theorem [MATH: (x+2)] is a factor of [MATH: f(x).]

We find the quotient when [MATH: f(x)] is divided by [MATH: (x+2)] using synthetic division.

[MATH: − 2|1|0|0|8; − 2|4|− 8; 1|− 2|4|0]

Thus, [MATH: f(x) = (x+2)(x^2-2x+4).]

To find the remaining two roots, we solve [MATH: x^2-2x+4 = 0] by completing the square:

[MATH: x^{2} − 2x + 4|= 0; x^{2} − 2x + 1 + 3|= 0; (x − 1)^{2} + 3|= 0; (x − 1)^{2}|= − 3; (x − 1)^{2}|= (sqrt(3)\textrm{i})^{2}; x − 1|= ± sqrt(3)\textrm{i}; x|= 1 ± sqrt(3)\textrm{i}]

Therefore, the solutions to our original equation are [MATH: x=-2, \, 1\pm \sqrt3\textrm{i}.]

sections.normalized_html: Find all of the solutions to [MATH: x^3-3x^2+12x-10 = 0] given that [MATH: x=1+3\text{i}] is a solution.
sections.readable_text: Find all of the solutions to [MATH: x^3-3x^2+12x-10 = 0] given that [MATH: x=1+3\text{i}] is a solution.

sections.normalized_html:
First, we let [MATH: f(x) = x^3-3x^2+12x-10.]

Since [MATH: f(x)] has real coefficients and [MATH: x_1=1+3\text{i}] is a root of [MATH: f(x),] the complex conjugate

[MATH: \overline{x_1}=\overline{1+3\textrm{i}}=1-3\text{i}] must also be a root of [MATH: f(x).]

Now, according to the factor theorem, [MATH: \big(x-(1+3\text{i})\big)\big(x-(1-3\text{i})\big)] is a factor of [MATH: f(x).] Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

[MATH: (x − (1 + 3\textrm{i}))(x − (1 − 3\textrm{i}))|=; x^{2} − (1 + 3\textrm{i} + 1 − 3\textrm{i})x + (1 + 3\textrm{i})(1 − 3\textrm{i})|=; x^{2} − 2x + (1^{2} − (3\textrm{i})^{2})|=; x^{2} − 2x + 10|.]

Next, we find the quotient when [MATH: f(x)] is divided by [MATH: x^2 - 2x + 10] using polynomial division.

[MATH: x^{2} − 2x + 10x − 1; x^{2} − 2x + 10x^{3} − 3x^{2} + 12x − 10; x^{2} − 2x + 10x^{3} − 2x^{2} + 10x_(―); x^{2} − 2x + 10x^{3} − 0x^{2} + 02x − 10; x^{2} − 2x + 10x^{3}− 0x^{2} + 02x − 10_(―); x^{2} − 2x + 10x^{3} − 3x^{2} + 12x − 10]

Thus, [MATH: f(x) = (x^2 - 2x + 10)(x-1).]

To find the remaining root, we set the linear factor equal to zero and solve for [MATH: x\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: x − 1 = 0⟹x = 1]

Therefore, the roots are [MATH: x=1, 1 \pm 3\textrm{i}.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The fundamental theorem of algebra tells us that any cubic polynomial with real coefficients has precisely three roots.

Content:
Moreover, since complex roots always come in complex conjugate pairs, it follows that all cubic polynomials with real coefficients must have at least one real root.

Content:
Therefore, if [MATH: p(x)] is a cubic polynomial with real coefficients, we must have one of the following two cases:

Content:
- [MATH: p(x)] has [MATH: 3] real roots (some of which might be repeated).
- [MATH: p(x)] has [MATH: 1] real root and [MATH: 2] complex conjugate roots.

Content:
We already know how to deal with the first case. In this lesson, we will focus on the second case.

---

Item 2 — Example: Finding the Roots of a Cubic Equation With Complex Roots Given One Real Root

Example Prompt:
Given that [MATH: x=-2] is a solution to the equation [MATH: x^3+8 = 0,] find the remaining solutions.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Let [MATH: f(x) = x^3+8.] Since [MATH: x=-2] is a root of [MATH: f(x),] then according to the factor theorem [MATH: (x+2)] is a factor of [MATH: f(x).]

We find the quotient when [MATH: f(x)] is divided by [MATH: (x+2)] using synthetic division.

[MATH: − 2|1|0|0|8; − 2|4|− 8; 1|− 2|4|0]

Thus, [MATH: f(x) = (x+2)(x^2-2x+4).]

To find the remaining two roots, we solve [MATH: x^2-2x+4 = 0] by completing the square:

[MATH: x^{2} − 2x + 4|= 0; x^{2} − 2x + 1 + 3|= 0; (x − 1)^{2} + 3|= 0; (x − 1)^{2}|= − 3; (x − 1)^{2}|= (sqrt(3)\textrm{i})^{2}; x − 1|= ± sqrt(3)\textrm{i}; x|= 1 ± sqrt(3)\textrm{i}]

Therefore, the solutions to our original equation are [MATH: x=-2, \, 1\pm \sqrt3\textrm{i}.]

Item 5 — Example: Finding the Roots of a Cubic Equation With Complex Roots Given One Complex Root

Find all of the solutions to [MATH: x^3-3x^2+12x-10 = 0] given that [MATH: x=1+3\text{i}] is a solution.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:

Since [MATH: f(x)] has real coefficients and [MATH: x_1=1+3\text{i}] is a root of [MATH: f(x),] the complex conjugate

[MATH: \overline{x_1}=\overline{1+3\textrm{i}}=1-3\text{i}]

Now, according to the factor theorem,
[MATH: \big(x-(1+3\text{i})\big)\big(x-(1-3\text{i})\big)]
is a factor of [MATH: f(x).] Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

[MATH: (x − (1 + 3\textrm{i}))(x − (1 − 3\textrm{i}))|=; x^{2} − (1 + 3\textrm{i} + 1 − 3\textrm{i})x + (1 + 3\textrm{i})(1 − 3\textrm{i})|=; x^{2} − 2x + (1^{2} − (3\textrm{i})^{2})|=; x^{2} − 2x + 10|.]

[MATH: x^{2} − 2x + 10x − 1; x^{2} − 2x + 10x^{3} − 3x^{2} + 12x − 10; x^{2} − 2x + 10x^{3} − 2x^{2} + 10x_(―); x^{2} − 2x + 10x^{3} − 0x^{2} + 02x − 10; x^{2} − 2x + 10x^{3}− 0x^{2} + 02x − 10_(―); x^{2} − 2x + 10x^{3} − 3x^{2} + 12x − 10]

Thus, [MATH: f(x) = (x^2 - 2x + 10)(x-1).]

To find the remaining root, we set the linear factor equal to zero and solve for [MATH: x\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: x − 1 = 0⟹x = 1]

Therefore, the roots are [MATH: x=1, 1 \pm 3\textrm{i}.]
